# Case: retry after ambiguous upload success

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Pending photo upload resumes after connectivity recovery.
- One logical upload must create at most one cloud object.

Technical design:
- Connectivity recovery enqueues a WorkManager UploadWorker.
- Worker retries on timeout.
- The design does not define an idempotency key, server deduplication, or uniqueness mechanism for one logical upload.
- Server may commit an upload before the client receives the response.

# Case: cancelled upload on network recovery

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Pending uploads resume after network recovery.
- The requirement does not say whether a user-cancelled upload remains pending or must stay cancelled.

Technical design:
- Network recovery enqueues every record whose local state is not SUCCESS.

Challenge the technical design without inventing the missing product behavior.

# Case: clean retry design

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Resume pending uploads after network recovery.
- Never create duplicate cloud objects for one logical upload.

Technical design:
- Each logical upload receives a persisted upload_id before enqueue.
- Every retry reuses the same upload_id.
- Cloud API PUT /objects/{upload_id} is idempotent and returns the existing object for a repeated upload_id.
- WorkManager may execute more than once; duplicate execution is explicitly tolerated.

# Case: unsupported recovery latency claim

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- 500 pending jobs must be scheduled within 30 seconds after network recovery.

Technical design:
- WorkManager is used for recovery scheduling.
- The document claims 500 jobs will always be scheduled within 30 seconds.
- No benchmark, load test, platform guarantee, or prototype evidence is supplied.

# Case: account identity constraint

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Resume pending uploads after connectivity recovery.

Existing system constraint:
- A pending upload must execute under the account identity that created it.

Technical design:
- Recovery queries every pending upload in the shared database and enqueues it under the currently active account.
- The design does not preserve originating account identity in the scheduled work.

# Case: process death between memory state and persistence

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- A pending upload must survive app process death.

Technical design:
1. UI marks an in-memory UploadSession as pending.
2. Worker is enqueued.
3. PendingUpload row is written asynchronously after enqueue.
4. Worker reads PendingUpload on start.

There is no transaction or recovery record covering process death between steps 2 and 3.

# Case: concurrent workers consume the same pending row

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- One logical upload produces at most one upload side effect.

Technical design:
- Two connectivity callbacks can each enqueue UploadWorker.
- Worker selects the first PENDING row, calls the upload API, then marks it RUNNING.
- There is no atomic claim/update, unique work key, or server idempotency contract.

# Case: partial local commit after remote success

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- A successful cloud upload must not be uploaded again.

Technical design:
- Upload API is called first.
- On HTTP success, local object state and upload history are written in two separate database transactions.
- Retry eligibility is determined from upload history.
- A crash may occur after object state is updated but before history is written.

# Case: database migration drops retry identity

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- Pending uploads created by the previous app version must continue after upgrade without duplication.

Technical design:
- Schema v12 replaces legacy task_key with a newly generated upload_id.
- Migration creates a new random upload_id for every old pending row.
- The server deduplicates by legacy task_key.

# Case: downstream API has ambiguous timeout semantics

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- A payment operation must not charge twice.

Existing API contract:
- POST /charge can return timeout after the server has accepted the charge.
- No idempotency token is supported.

Technical design:
- Client retries POST /charge on any timeout.

# Case: out-of-order callbacks overwrite newer state

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- UI must display the latest upload state.

Technical design:
- Each worker posts progress and completion callbacks to a shared observer.
- The observer writes callback state directly to the row without sequence/version comparison.
- Network retry can start a new worker before the old worker's delayed callback arrives.

# Case: planned mechanism correctly exists only in design

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Retry must be idempotent.

Technical design:
- The feature will add persisted operation_id on the client and Idempotency-Key support in the new server endpoint.
- API contract in the design states repeated keys return the original result.

Repository context:
- The current released code has no operation_id because this feature has not been implemented yet.

Do not treat absence from current code as evidence that the planned mechanism is missing.

# Case: inferred historical constraint

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Cache can be cleared during logout.

Context:
- One historical bug suggests an old flow once retained draft data across logout.
- There is no ADR, current code contract, or requirement proving that retaining drafts is still an invariant.

Technical design:
- Logout clears all cached draft data.

Treat the historical bug only as a challenge seed until the supposed constraint is verified.

# Case: architecture-stage design should not be judged as LLD

Design Stage: architecture

Accepted requirement:
- Upload service must survive client restarts and support offline recovery.

Architecture design:
- Durable local work queue owns pending intent.
- Background scheduler consumes the durable queue after constraints recover.
- Cloud write boundary uses an idempotent operation identity.
- Detailed database columns, transaction calls, and class names are intentionally deferred to detailed design.

# Case: architecture omits required regional failover

Design Stage: architecture

Accepted requirement:
- Upload API must remain available after loss of one region.

Architecture design:
- All upload traffic, metadata, and queue state are hosted in one region.
- No second region, replication, failover, or degraded-mode mechanism is defined.

# Case: cache becomes accidental source of truth

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- After reconnect, server state is authoritative for shared album membership.

Technical design:
- Membership is loaded from an in-memory cache.
- Offline edits mutate the cache.
- On reconnect the cached object is written to server without version check or re-read.

# Case: removal breaks an existing dependency

Design Stage: architecture

Accepted requirement:
- Replace the legacy connectivity service with platform callbacks.

Existing system constraint:
- SyncScheduler also consumes the legacy service's durable network-generation token to suppress stale work after network changes.

Technical design:
- Deletes the legacy connectivity service and replaces only the boolean online/offline callback.
- No replacement is provided for network-generation identity.

# Case: invalid exactly-once platform assumption

Design Stage: high_level

Accepted requirement:
- Retried background work must not duplicate server-side side effects.

Technical design:
- States that WorkManager guarantees exactly-once execution, so no application idempotency is required.

Platform context supplied to the review:
- WorkManager provides persistent scheduling and retries; application work may be re-run and must tolerate repeated execution.

context.platform.md: WorkManager work can be stopped and retried; application logic must tolerate repeated execution and should not assume exactly-once side effects.

# Case: architecture owner must choose consistency model

Design Stage: architecture

Accepted requirement:
- Shared album edits from two devices must eventually converge and must not silently discard an accepted edit.

Architecture design:
- Lists two viable approaches: server revision compare-and-reject, or CRDT merge.
- The design intentionally leaves the choice unresolved.
- Both could satisfy the requirement but have different implementation and operational consequences.

# Case: existing retry path is already idempotent

Design Stage: detailed

Accepted requirement:
- Retrying media metadata update must not create duplicate revisions.

Existing design and contract:
- Client persists mutation_id before the first request.
- Every retry sends the same mutation_id.
- Server stores mutation_id with the committed revision and returns that revision for repeated mutation_id.
- Integration tests cover response loss followed by retry.
